subject: Copywriting
title: Features Tell, Benefits Sell
description: A quick win: understand Features Tell, Benefits Sell.

hook.text: 'This drill has a 1/4-inch bit' is a feature. 'This drill makes a 1/4-inch hole' is a benefit.

buildup.text: Features describe the product. Benefits describe what the product does for the reader. Sales letters sell benefits.

discovery.text: Features Tell, Benefits Sell reveals the mechanism or argument that changes the picture.

twist.text: Some audiences want features: engineers, developers, and technical buyers. Know when to lead with specs vs outcomes.

climax.text: The master technique: state the feature, then immediately translate it into a benefit.

punchline.text: People buy holes, not drills. Translate every feature into a benefit.

quiz.question: What is the difference between a feature and a benefit?
options: Features cost money; benefits are free
Features describe the product; benefits describe what it does for the reader

details.summary: Features describe what a product is; benefits explain what it does for the buyer. 'Titanium frame' is a feature. 'Lightweight enough to carry all day without fatigue' is a benefit. Great sales letters translate every feature into a benefit the reader can feel.
details.whyItMatters: The feature-benefit distinction is copywriting's most fundamental principle. Mastering it transforms technical descriptions into emotional appeals that drive purchasing decisions.
takeaways: Features are facts about the product; benefits are outcomes for the buyer
The 'so what?' test converts features into benefits
Benefits sell emotionally; features justify the purchase rationally

faq.question: How do you convert a feature into a benefit?
faq.answer: Ask 'so what?' after every feature until you reach an emotional outcome. '256GB storage' → 'So what?' → 'You'll never run out of space for photos and videos' → 'So what?' → 'You'll capture every important memory without worrying about deleting old ones.'

faq.question: Should features ever be included in sales copy?
faq.answer: Yes — after the benefit. Benefits create desire; features justify the purchase rationally. 'Capture every memory without worry (256GB storage)' uses both. Analytical buyers need features as permission to buy what the benefits made them want.
